findings.issue: fetchJson caches the promise for every URL even when it resolves to null (network error or non-ok response), so a transient API failure at cold start permanently poisons the in-memory cache — e.g. getHomeCatalog would bake in entries with empty types and null sprites until restart, and missing records become indistinguishable from genuine 404s
findings.suggestion: Only store the promise in the cache on success (or delete the entry when it resolves to null), distinguish non-ok responses from thrown errors, and log failures instead of silently returning null

findings.issue: The home routeLoader returns the entire 1025-entry catalog, which Qwik serializes into every home-page HTML payload (~150KB+) because useComputed$ filters it on the client
findings.suggestion: Filter/paginate server-side inside routeLoader$ from the request's url params (the framework-native URL-driven loader pattern), returning only the 48 visible cards plus counts; keep client-side filtering only if the payload tradeoff is consciously accepted and trimmed

findings.issue: Filter state is written with window.history.replaceState (three near-identical handlers at lines 64, 80, 103), bypassing Qwik City's router, and the game select at app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:417 does a full window.location.assign — the router's own location state goes stale and SPA navigation is lost
findings.suggestion: Use Qwik City's navigation (useNavigate()/loc.url via the useLocation signal or location.href assignment the router intercepts) so URL updates flow through the framework

findings.issue: 404 handling is a hand-rolled sentinel ({notFound:true}) plus a catch-all route, so missing resources respond with HTTP 200 and skip the framework's 404 pipeline that current Qwik City docs recommend
findings.suggestion: Add src/routes/404.tsx for unmatched URLs and throw ev.error(404) from the loaders when a resource is missing, so the server responds with the correct status

findings.issue: Client components import pure formatters from data.ts (app/src/components/ui.tsx:2), dragging the module-scope global-store initialization into the client bundle (verified in dist/build/q-DivkbU9H.js:1) — a leaky server/client boundary that only works because tree-shaking happens to drop the fetchers
findings.suggestion: Move humanize/displayDex/formatValue into a client-safe src/lib/format.ts and keep data.ts strictly server-only

findings.issue: API records are typed as any throughout (TypeOption.record: any, record: any in every accessor), so payload shape changes fail silently at runtime
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API resources used (species, pokemon, type, move, ability) and annotate the accessors

findings.issue: Three near-duplicate onInput$/onChange$ handlers each repeat the signal-update, page-reset and replaceState sequence
findings.suggestion: Extract one setFilter$ helper that takes the field and new value and centralizes the URL/URL-sync behavior

findings.issue: Selects set both value={} and per-option selected attributes, a redundant pattern that invites hydration/controlled-state confusion
findings.suggestion: Pick one mechanism (the selected attribute on options is what actually survives SSR; drop the value prop or vice versa) and use it consistently

summary: A competent, recognisably idiomatic Qwik City app: route loaders, head functions and SSR setup follow the framework's own patterns, and the code is easy to find one's way around. The main merge blockers are the silent, permanently cached fetch failures in the shared data layer, the hand-rolled URL/404 handling that bypasses the router and the framework's 404 pipeline, and the full 1025-entry catalog serialized into every home-page payload. I'd ask for one focused round of changes before approving.
